source.title: Comparing Text Representations: A Theory-Driven Approach

page_placements.theme: Frozen-representation probes separate semantic and arbitrary-label fitting

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares the DDC of real and randomly relabeled text datasets under fixed representations, and separately reports two-layer network classification results on MNIST and text tasks. It does not test the original random-image-labeling setup; its main method analyzes representation-label alignment without training classifiers.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own DDC comparisons of real versus random labelings for NLI representations, and its reported trained-network comparison on MNLI bag-of-words. Cited findings from prior work were excluded. The study does not test random image labels, shuffled or noise inputs, label-noise sweeps, regularization, or learning order.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation–label alignment using DDC and reports classifiers' dev accuracy on true labels. It does not measure random-label fitting, compare training times for real and random labels, or provide an argument against any claim version. DDC differences alone cannot establish these effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose DDC calibrated against random-label distributions to quantify representation–task alignment and supplement held-out accuracy without training classifiers for that analysis. They do not claim to establish random-label memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a DDC analysis of representation-label alignment rather than training the original random-labeling intervention; limited classifier training results use true labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Representation and dataset change the real-versus-random DDC comparison; the paper reports that BOW/GloVe behave differently from pretrained MLM representations and that WNLI differs from MNLI, QNLI, and SNLI.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNLI, BOW shows little DDC separation between real and random labels; GloVe gives real labels higher DDC than all sampled random labelings; pretrained MLM representations give real labels substantially lower DDC than random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation–label alignment, measured by DDC relative to random-label distributions, depends on the text representation.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer classifiers achieve true-label MNLI dev accuracies of 43.8%, 67.1%, and 96.6% using BOW, pretrained RoBERTa-large, and MNLI-fine-tuned RoBERTa-large representations, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained and fine-tuned contextual representations improve downstream MNLI classification relative to BOW.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The central evidence is a theoretical DDC measure rather than training error on randomized labels. Network classification results are reported as dev accuracy; no random-label training accuracy or test error is provided. Some comparisons are summarized in figures and distributions of sampled random labelings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results left out. Other DDC measurements about alternative Stack Exchange labelings and NLI datasets/representations were not extracted because they do not directly test the listed random-label fitting claim beyond the MNLI evidence captured here.

untested.parts: Random-label training error, chance test performance, and fitting with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Real-versus-random-label training-time ratios and convergence as label corruption increases. Reported computation times do not make these comparisons.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error trajectories across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels. Static DDC comparisons do not measure this ordering.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 limits_scope verdict. Measuring a different construct leaves V1 untested; it does not qualify its scope. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random labelings of NLI text data through DDC and reports a two-layer network trained on MNLI bag-of-words; does not establish zero training error on random labels or test error at chance, nor test random image labels.

relation.reason: The study discusses fitting arbitrary labels and theoretical connections to SGD convergence, but reports no random-label fitting outcomes or real-versus-random training-time comparison.

tranche.reason: DDC measures representation–label alignment, a different construct from the claim versions. The reported classifier accuracies use true labels; the study neither tests nor uses random-label memorization.

source_check.notes: All three accuracies are best dev results across four learning rates after classifier training on 10,000 examples. NLI analysis uses entailment and contradiction classes; these are not full three-class MNLI results or evidence of random-label memorization.

reader_labels.reason: The paper finds representation-dependent differences between real and random labelings, but DDC does not measure zero training error or chance test error on a trained model (R1–R4).
